title: 500 Internal Server Error
description: Resolve HTTP 500 errors — often caused by .htaccess rules, PHP crashes, corrupt core files, or server misconfiguration.

steps.title: Check Server and PHP Error Logs
steps.instructions: Review the host error log, PHP-FPM log, and wp-content/debug.log. Note the timestamp, file path, and line number of the first error after the 500 started.

steps.title: Test .htaccess Rules
steps.instructions: Rename .htaccess to .htaccess.bak and reload the site. If it works, regenerate permalinks or fix malformed rewrite rules. Restore a clean WordPress .htaccess block.

steps.title: Confirm PHP Version Compatibility
steps.instructions: Ensure PHP meets WordPress minimums and your plugins' requirements. Switch PHP version in hosting panel if a recent upgrade coincides with the 500 error.

steps.title: Isolate Plugin or Theme Fault
steps.instructions: Deactivate all plugins and switch to a default theme via SFTP or database. Re-enable one at a time to find the component triggering the 500.

steps.title: Reinstall WordPress Core Files
steps.instructions: Upload fresh copies of wp-admin and wp-includes from a matching WordPress release. Do not overwrite wp-config.php or wp-content.

steps.title: Fix File and Folder Permissions
steps.instructions: Directories should typically be 755 and files 644. wp-config.php is often 440 or 600. Incorrect permissions on .htaccess or wp-config can cause 500 errors.

steps.title: Verify Site Recovery
steps.instructions: Confirm HTTP 200 on homepage, admin login, and REST API. Monitor error logs for 24 hours after the fix.
